worked_solution:
We know that the denominator $\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+{e}^{x}$ is positive for all values of $x.$ So, we can multiply both sides of the inequality by $\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+{e}^{x}$ and solve the resulting inequality as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x+4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+{e}^{x}} & >\frac{x+10}{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+{e}^{x}} \\ (\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{3x+4}{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+{e}^{x}} & >(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+{e}^{x})\cdot \frac{x+10}{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}+1)+{e}^{x}} \\ 3x+4 & >x+10 \\ 2x & >6 \\ x & >\,3\end{aligned}
$$
